To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cTfMAb domain acts as a molecular “Trojan horse” to deliver a biologic TNF inhibitor (TNFI) across the blood–brain barrie (BBB), and that intravenous TNFI treatment is therapeutic after delayed administration in experimental stroke.
we have developed a novel biologic TNF inhibitor that crosses the BBB and protects the brain from stroke.

a biologic TNF inhibitor, which cannot be used in stroke treatment because of poor brain penetration, can be engineered for BBB penetration and is therapeutic when administered intravenously up to 90 minutes after the onset of stroke.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of biologic TNF inhibitors that can be used as novel neuroprotective agents in stroke and other neurological disorders.
the development of a novel biologic TNF inhibitor for stroke treatment, which can be administered intravenously, and is effective after a delayed treatment.
the development of a new stroke treatment that can be administered after stroke onset.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cTfMAb-TNFI fusion protein is neuroprotective in experimental stroke.
the IgG-TnFR fusion protein is neuroprotective in the mouse MCAO model of ischemic stroke, whereas etanercept is not.
the fusion protein is therapeutic for experimental stroke after delayed administration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IgG-TNF receptor fusion protein is therapeutic for stroke when administered up to 90 minutes after stroke.
the fusion protein is a novel therapeutic agent for stroke and that it has the potential to be developed into a new stroke treatment.
a BBB-penetrant TNFR fusion protein, when administered intravenously up to 90 minutes after stroke onset, can reduce stroke size and improve neurologic function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BBB-penetrant IgG-TNFRII fusion protein is therapeutic for stroke after intravenous administration in mice.
a biologic TNF inhibitor, which cannot cross the BBB, can be reengineeered for BBB penetration by fusion with the cTfMAb, and this fusion protein is therapeutic in experimental stroke.
the cTfMAb-TNRF fusion protein is a promising new stroke therapy.
